This approach is useful when a target language lacks plentiful labeled data, particularly for specific domains. arxiv-1912-07729.title: Incorporating Unlabeled Data into Distributionally-Robust Learning
arxiv-1912-07729.creator: Charlie Frogner frogner@mit.edu, Sebastian Claici sclaici@mit.edu, Edward Chien edchien@mit.edu, Justin Solomon jsolomon@mit.edu
arxiv-1912-07729.description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Charlie Frogner frogner@mit.edu, Sebastian Claici sclaici@mit.edu, Edward Chien edchien@mit.edu, Justin Solomon jsolomon@mit.edu. We study a robust alternative to empirical risk minimization called distributionally robust learning (DRL), in which one learns to perform against an adversary who can choose the data distribution from a specified set of distributions. We illustrate a problem with current DRL formulations, which rely on an overly broad definition of allowed distributions for the adversary, leading to learned classifiers that are unable to predict with any confidence.

arxiv-2105-05638.title: On the photometric metallicity of Oosterhoff-type I and II RRab stars On the photometric metallicity of Oosterhoff-type I and II RRab stars – 2021
arxiv-2105-05638.creator: J. Jurcsik, G. Hajdu, Á. Juhász
arxiv-2105-05638.description: Abstract We are revising the consistency of photometric metallicity formulae widely used for fundamental-mode RR Lyrae (RRab) variables, based on their V V - and I I -band light curves, published by Jurcsik and Kovács (1996) and Smolec (2005), respectively.

arxiv-2109-13484.title: Trapping and binding by dephasing
arxiv-2109-13484.creator: K. Mukherjee, S. Poddar, S. Wüster
arxiv-2109-13484.description: Abstract Binding and trapping of particles usually rely on conservative forces, described by unitary quantum dynamics. We show that both can also arise solely from spatially dependent dephasing, the simplest type of decoherence. This can be based on continuous weak position measurements in only selected regions of space, for which we propose a practical realisation.

arxiv-2111-06801.title: Benchmarking deep generative models for diverse antibody sequence design
arxiv-2111-06801.creator: Igor Melnyk, Payel Das, Vijil Chenthamarakshan, Aurelie Lozano
arxiv-2111-06801.description: Abstract Computational protein design, i.e. inferring novel and diverse protein sequences consistent with a given structure, remains a major unsolved challenge. Recently, deep generative models that learn from sequences alone or from sequences and structures jointly have shown impressive performance on this task. However, those models appear limited in terms of modeling structural constraints, capturing enough sequence diversity, or both.

arxiv-2308-04458.title: The number of primes in short intervals and numerical calculations for Harman’s sieve
arxiv-2308-04458.creator: Runbo Li
arxiv-2308-04458.description: Abstract . The author gives nontrivial upper and lower bounds for the number of primes in the interval [ x − x θ , x ] [x-x^{\theta},x] for some 0.52 ⩽ θ < 0.525 0.52\leqslant\theta<0.525 , showing that the interval [ x − x 0.52 , x ] [x-x^{0.52},x] contains prime numbers for all sufficiently large x x .

arxiv-2312-02729.title: High- K K isomers in a self-consistent mean-field approach with the Gogny force
arxiv-2312-02729.creator: L. M. Robledo
arxiv-2312-02729.description: Abstract High- K K isomeric states in even-even and odd-mass nuclei are described within a mean-field framework with full blocking and using the finite range Gogny force. Theoretical calculations of low energy spectra of several nuclei across the nuclear chart are compared with equal filling approximation results and experimental data.

arxiv-2407-14154.title: Where is the Testbed for my Federated Learning Research?
arxiv-2407-14154.creator: Janez Božič 1 , Amândio R. Faustino 1 , Boris Radovič 1 , Marco Canini , Veljko Pejović
arxiv-2407-14154.description: Abstract Progressing beyond centralized AI is of paramount importance, yet, distributed AI solutions, in particular various federated learning (FL) algorithms, are often not comprehensively assessed, which prevents the research community from identifying the most promising approaches and practitioners from being convinced that a certain solution is deployment-ready.

arxiv-2503-05463.title: Search for Higgs boson exotic decays into Lorentz-boosted light bosons in the four- τ \tau final state at s = 13 ​ TeV \sqrt{s}=13\,\mathrm{TeV} with the ATLAS detector
arxiv-2503-05463.description: Abstract A search for exotic decays of the Higgs boson into a pair of low-mass scalars that subsequently decay into τ \tau -leptons, H → a ​ a → τ + ​ τ − ​ τ + ​ τ − H\rightarrow aa\rightarrow\tau^{+}\tau^{-}\tau^{+}\tau^{-} , is presented.

arxiv-2511-09732.title: Theory and algorithms for clusters of cycles in graphs for material networks
arxiv-2511-09732.creator: Perrin E. Ruth, Maria Cameron
arxiv-2511-09732.description: Abstract Analysis of complex networks, particularly material networks such as the carbon skeleton of hydrocarbons generated in hydrocarbon pyrolysis in carbon-rich systems, is essential for effectively describing, modeling, and predicting their features. An important and the most challenging part of this analysis is the extraction and effective description of cycles, when many of them coalesce into complex clusters.

pmc-11399644.creator: Gill Hubbard, Diane Dixon, Marie Johnston, Chantal den Daas
pmc-11399644.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). ObjectivesTo investigate the relationship between long-term condition (LTC) status and adherence to protective behaviours against infectious disease (face covering, physical distancing, hand hygiene).Study designRepresentative cross-sectional observational survey in summer 2020 in Scotland.MethodsIndependent variable is LTC status (LTC, disability, no LTC); dependent variable is adherence to protective behaviours (face covering, hand hygiene, social distancing); moderator variables are age, gender and area deprivation; mediator variables are perceived threat and psychological distress.

pmc-11425457.title: S13-2: ”I enjoyed the camaraderie, the atmosphere and the inclusiveness of parkrun”: A qualitative study to explore mental wellbeing in middle-aged men at parkrun Ireland
pmc-11425457.creator: Allison Dunne, Helen Quirk, Alice Bullas, Steve Haake
pmc-11425457.description: PurposeMiddle-aged men in Ireland are a population who are known to be at high risk of poor mental wellbeing and suicide. One health promotion strategy for this population is to participate in community initiatives which combine a purposeful activity with social contact to support physical, mental and social wellbeing.

pmc-12380344.title: Study on the influencing factors of ecological spatial grouping optimization in the huangshan region based on entropy weight topsis
pmc-12380344.creator: Le Zhang, Qiqi Rao, Mingxia Yuan, Yanlong Guo
pmc-12380344.description: This study evaluates and analyzes the influencing factors of ecological spatial configuration optimization in the Greater Huangshan Region. By identifying and assessing these factors, it aims to reveal the mechanisms underlying ecological space optimization in the area. The findings provide a theoretical foundation for promoting high-quality development and optimizing ecological spatial governance policies in the Greater Huangshan Region.

pmc-12419619.title: Prevalence and predictors of viral load non-suppression among adolescents on dolutegravir-based antiretroviral therapy: A cross-sectional study from three urban clinics, Soroti City

pmc-12563741.title: Beyond Antibiotics: Repurposing Non-Antibiotic Drugs as Novel Antibacterial Agents to Combat Resistance
pmc-12563741.creator: Gagan Tiwana, Ian Edwin Cock, Stephen Maxwell Taylor, Matthew James Cheesman
pmc-12563741.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The escalating global threat of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) necessitates innovative therapeutic strategies beyond traditional antibiotic development. Drug repurposing offers a rapid, cost-effective approach by identifying new antibacterial applications for existing non-antibiotic drugs with established safety profiles. Emerging evidence indicates that diverse classes of non-antibiotic drugs, including non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), statins, antipsychotics, calcium channel blockers and antidepressants, exhibit intrinsic antibacterial activity, or potentiate antibiotic efficacy.

pmc-12738840.title: Challenges and opportunities for oncology drug repurposing informed by synthetic lethality
pmc-12738840.creator: Michael Vermeulen, Andrew W Craig, Tomas Babak
pmc-12738840.description: Although two-thirds of cancers arise from loss-of-function mutations in tumor suppressor genes, there are few approved targeted therapies linked to these alterations. Synthetic lethality offers a promising strategy to treat such cancers by targeting vulnerabilities unique to cancer cells with these mutations.

pmc-13196164.title: Children’s experiences of willpower and self-regulation: a phenomenological study of emotions, strategies, and metaphorical meanings in school-aged children
pmc-13196164.creator: Esma Gokkoyun, Ebru Kilicarslan
pmc-13196164.description: BackgroundWillpower and self-regulation are central developmental capacities associated with children’s academic success, psychosocial adjustment, and long-term well-being. Although these constructs have been widely studied in preschoolers and adults, limited research has explored how school-aged children themselves perceive and experience willpower in their everyday lives.

pmc-13241842.title: Symptom benchmarks of improved quality of life among military veterans with PTSD☆
pmc-13241842.creator: Paula P. Schnurr, Carole A. Lunney, Kathleen M. Chard, Josef I. Ruzek, Brian P. Marx, Thomas M. Crow
pmc-13241842.description: ObjectiveTo optimize treatment outcome and promote recovery, it is necessary to understand how clinical indicators of improvement translate into meaningful differences in the lives of individuals with posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD). Prior research has suggested that treatment response alone is insufficient and that more substantial improvement is needed, but data are limited.

pmc-13408418.title: Solvent-Dependent Green Synthesis of ZnO Nanopowders Using Mitragyna speciosa Leaf Extract: Impact on Piezo-Photocatalytic and Antibacterial
pmc-13408418.creator: Thanyapa Sanyen, Maneerat Songpanit, Thanaphon Kansaard, Supamas Wirunchit, Sutee Chutipaijit, Keiichi N. Ishihara, Hideyuki Okumura, Wisanu Pecharapa, Wanichaya Mekprasart, Kanokthip Boonyarattanakalin
pmc-13408418.description: ZnO nanopowders were synthesized via a solvent-mediated green route using Mitragyna speciosa Korth. leaf extract as reducing and stabilizing agents. Deionized water and methanol were employed to tailor the phytochemical composition of the extracts. The influence of extract concentration (5–20 mL) and solvent polarity on structural, morphological, and functional properties was systematically investigated.

pmc-13625619.title: TEMPO-oxidised cellulose nanofibrils from bacterial cellulose: how the cellulose source influences the gelation mechanisms
pmc-13625619.creator: Julien Schmitt, Vincenzo Calabrese, Kazi M. Zakir Hossain, Janet L. Scott, Karen J. Edler
pmc-13625619.description: TEMPO-oxidation of cellulose is used to form water-dispersible, negatively-charged nanofibrils. It is known that the type of cellulose source influences the yield of TEMPO-oxidation, the number of carboxylate groups and the crystallinity index. In this paper, we aim to demonstrate its influence on water-based formulations.

pmc-13630932.title: When fitness testing becomes personal: achievement emotions and participation orientations in compulsory university physical education
pmc-13630932.creator: Chao Wang, Wenqiang Zheng, Qi Li
pmc-13630932.description: Fitness testing can support learning when pedagogically embedded, but public, graded enactment can expose students' bodies to comparison and judgement. Prior research documents negative experiences but does not explain why similar instances of low performance are interpreted as repairable, personally diminishing, or procedurally unfair.
